name: Morocco
headline: Morocco: +4.9% growth in 2025, 0.8% inflation, debt 67% of GDP
sections: Morocco is a $184 billion economy (2025), the world's 59th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $11K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.9% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 13.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 21.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 67% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 72% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 93% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 62% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 75.5 years (2024). Population: 37.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
